result.summary: gjson v1.18.0 is a pure-Go JSON path query library. Its surface file gjson.go contains parsing, validation and modifier functions, plus an init that only builds an in-memory map of modifier functions. I checked for I/O, network, exec, environment access, encoded payloads and runtime hooking and found none; the only unsafe use is the library's well-known zero-copy string/byte conversion.

findings.title: unsafe pointer casts for zero-copy string/byte conversion
findings.detail: The package uses unsafe.Pointer to convert between strings and byte slices without copying (getBytes, stringBytes, bytesString) and to compute result indexes (fillIndex). This is the upstream library's long-standing performance technique. It is local memory handling with no external effect, so it is not shady.

findings.title: init registers modifier table only
findings.detail: init() only fills the built-in modifiers map with local pure functions (pretty, ugly, reverse, this, flatten, join, valid, keys, values, tostr, fromstr, group, dig). None of them perform I/O, run programs or have other side effects.
